tasks.short: Compare production costs statistically across designs

steps.what: Define statistical comparisons and verify costs for sustainable and nonsustainable designs
Calculate specified statistical summaries and production cost comparisons
Interpret statistical studies and explain limitations of design cost comparisons

tasks.design: Configure reproducible statistical calculations in {SPREADSHEET} from a verified study specification. Keep comparability decisions, assumptions and interpretation with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual calculation can be repeated while design definitions and cost boundaries change.
tasks.enabler_now: Native statistical functions and protected formulas can rerun defined comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: Avoid confounding production scale, material choice and sustainability classifications.
tasks.human_edge: Identify when an apparent cost difference is not a valid comparison.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated computation, unchanged authority to interpret costs.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: specified statistical calculations can be rerun deterministically; this is not evidence of valid sustainability classification or a local saving.

assumptions: Boundary is statistical production-cost comparison, excluding design creation and environmental impact certification.

The technician produces design versions, classification rationale, cost boundary, currency/date basis, quantities, observation units, exclusions, formulas and comparison method in s1. Extraction, classification and source capture retain its full 35%; missing comparability evidence returns to manual investigation.
s2 uses only verified s1 data and rejects incompatible units or unspecified methods. No free sustainable-design flag is assumed.
Test native statistics before custom code. Existing automatic calculations earn no labour saving.
unknowns: Cost comparability and existing statistical tools
research_questions: How much repeated computation remains after input verification and comparability assessment?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+30=65; gross=35, incremental=8, net=27. Range 0-10 allows existing calculations or difficult cost normalisation to consume most computation gains; interpretation is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Oversee equipment start-up, characterization, qualification or release under engineering direction

tasks.design: Keep physical oversight and qualification judgement with the technician under engineering direction. {DOCS} contains current instructions and evidence; no separate report-assembly baseline is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A completed checklist does not establish that startup behaviour is acceptable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing test plans and records support the work; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise abnormal behaviour and determine when engineering escalation is needed.
tasks.human_edge: Relate test evidence to actual equipment behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Oversight duties and final release authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: DewesoftX records test data and produces reports; this does not establish automatic equipment qualification or release.

assumptions: Boundary is technician oversight and recommendation, excluding physical installation and the responsible engineer's final release decision.

The engineer supplies approved test conditions and startup authorisation before activity. Test personnel and equipment produce observations during execution before interpretation; the technician verifies configuration, measurements and deviations within s1. No free ready-for-release flag is assumed.
Uncertain results return to the responsible engineer under the existing process. Test native recording facilities before custom tools; none is added.
Zero incremental upkeep follows from unchanged oversight, equipment and authority.
research_questions: Is routine report assembly a measurable activity distinct from physical qualification oversight?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, incremental=0; net=0. Successful startup and unexpected qualification results retain human oversight; final engineering release is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop infrastructure for new manufacturing processes

steps.what: Develop manufacturing infrastructure proposals against process and site constraints
Integrate infrastructure changes and verify interfaces under approved engineering instructions

tasks.design: Keep site-specific infrastructure development and integration human. {DOCS} and {OPS_SYSTEM} support current engineering instructions and observed interfaces; no generic software-integration saving is assigned to physical infrastructure.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manufacturing interfaces depend on physical layout, utilities and process constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing engineering methods support the task; no new automation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Reconcile the proposed infrastructure with actual site conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Notice an installation or interface mismatch before it becomes an operational problem.
tasks.altitude: Development duties and engineering decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Mechanical, utility and control interface requirements

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: developing physical manufacturing infrastructure includes site-specific judgement and integration; a generic software automation saving would not represent this task.

assumptions: Boundary is technician proposal and integration assistance, excluding engineer design approval, contractor installation labour and final release.

The technician captures site conditions, interface dimensions, utilities, loads and unresolved constraints in s1. The responsible engineer produces approval and installation limits after the proposal and before s2. Verification and clarification remain in the full shares; no free compatible-interface flag is assumed.
The technician checks current authorisation before each permitted integration action in s2; changes beyond it return to engineering.
Test native engineering tools before custom code. Incremental upkeep is zero because no new tooling or transferred duty is proposed.
unknowns: Infrastructure scope and technician installation authority
research_questions: Is there repeated drawing or list preparation separate from physical infrastructure development?

already_counted.description: Authorisation checks, integration and interface verification

approvals.approved_version: Exact engineering instruction revision, authorised change, equipment, site condition and interface scope checked before each action; changes void approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100, incremental=0, net=0. Familiar and novel process integrations retain proposal and physical verification work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify production schedules, worker constraints, machine capacity and anticipated delays
Assemble planning constraints and calculate capacity balances for work assignments
Aid in planning work assignments and explain operational trade-offs

tasks.design: Configure a capacity comparison in {SPREADSHEET} from a verified planning brief. Keep interpretation of worker constraints and assignment recommendations human; the production supervisor retains assignment authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Planning support can involve repeated collation and capacity arithmetic.
tasks.enabler_now: Native tables and formulas can show explicit constraints without ranking workers or allocating duties.
tasks.still_hard: Judge anticipated disruption and the suitability of an assignment for a person.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise practical and interpersonal constraints absent from nominal capacity.
tasks.altitude: Less planning collation, unchanged recommendation and assignment authority.

evidence.claim: The digest identifies EU AI Act and Dutch works-council implications for AI work allocation based on worker performance; this design keeps allocation human and introduces no performance-scoring model.
Model knowledge: capacity collation can use explicit formulas without automating assignment judgement; local savings remain unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is planning assistance, excluding supervisor assignment decisions and employee work execution.

In s1 the technician produces schedule revision, required tasks, duration assumptions, available machine hours, delay assumptions and supervisor-verified worker constraints. Elicitation, interpretation and capture retain the full 35%; missing constraints require manual clarification. No free qualified-worker or available-machine flag is assumed.
s2 only assembles supplied constraints and capacity arithmetic; it neither infers performance nor proposes person rankings. Supervisor assignment work is unchanged.
Test native production planning views before custom code; confirm applicable national consultation and access requirements before changing records.
unknowns: Current planning automation and source of worker constraints
research_questions: Can collation be reduced without introducing new employee assessment or assignment work?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+40=75; gross=25, incremental=7, net=18. Range 0-7 allows changing worker constraints or existing capacity views to consume most collation savings; assignment judgement stays human.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reproducible cost and capacity comparisons support unchanged physical oversight and engineering judgement.
reach: Explain statistical cost limitations and practical assignment constraints to engineering colleagues.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who can reproduce planning evidence while recognising the limits of numerical comparisons.
